result.summary:
CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR, WF-03 step 03 (hard gate on CODE-DESIGNER) for ISS-0002. VERDICT: FAIL. One MEDIUM finding (F1, blocking) and seven LOW findings (F2-F8, cheap to fix in the same edit). Everything else I was asked to verify passes. I changed nothing in the design or in code; every run used scratch copies.

DESIGN UNDER REVIEW. docs/design/REQ-002-idea-verdict.md, version 4 round 2, 1329 lines, sha256 b9041f8b5acd111772d2175790beec99f5696a29e2393c52b52cb8e583df1c32, mtime 2026-10-01T02:31:05Z. Re-hashed at the end of my work: unchanged. Requirement text read from docs/requirements.yaml (sha256 4450091a..., unchanged). The REQ-002 block (lines 277-315, 39 lines) has sha256 99b10223..., the same block that design section 9.1 says it was checked against.

IN SHORT. The design is complete and can be built without guessing. Write order (proposed-actions.json, apply-report.json, STATE.md last), commit point (the STATE.md rename), rollback (hard links, reverse order), temp names (.<name>.sai-tmp, .<name>.sai-old, folder .<name>.sai-tmp/), leftover handling (refuse, never delete), the E_WRITE message catalogue and the exit codes (0, 1, 2; E_WRITE is 1, P12 is 2) are all stated. Every clause of criterion 11 and every touched criterion maps to named tests. There is no implementation code. The write set is respected. Six pre-fix claims reproduced exactly. It fails on the one point ORCH asked me to judge: the design never says that validate follows a symlinked run folder and that this was accepted.

FINDINGS

F1 MEDIUM, blocking. Sections 5.4 (table), 10 and 12 (row Q11), 11. The read-through of a symlinked run folder is not stated anywhere in the design.
- What the design says: 5.4 has a row only for the write side ("запись идёт по ссылке, код 0 (W13)", which becomes E_WRITE ELOOP). Section 9.1 (a test-mapping table) notes that resolveRunDir compares paths. The Q11 rows say "папка прогона только внутри runs/" and speak only about writes. A grep of the design for a line holding both "validate" and a link word finds nothing. ORCH's ruling cites 5.4 as the place where the acceptance is stated; 5.4 does not contain it. The designer raised it only as open question 5 in the handoff, not in the design.
- What the code does (my run, W13 below; the design leaves validate.js and cli.js unchanged): with runs/WF06-20260925-01 a symlink to a valid run outside <root>, "validate" exits 0, "OK WF06-20260925-01 (stage review)". So validate and the read phase of apply-verdict read files outside <root>.
- Why it matters: a reader of Q11 takes the run folder as confined to the project. BACKEND-DEV or REVIEWER may "fix" resolveRunDir or validate (both inside the write set), or TEST-DESIGNER may expect E_USAGE. AP-014 says a same-class site that is knowingly left alone must be recorded where the next reader looks.
- Fix (text only; no new test is needed for PASS). (a) Add a row to the 5.4 table: "validate и чтение apply-verdict до записи; runs/<RUN-ID> — ссылка на папку вне <root>". Now: reads through the link, validate exits 0. After ISS-0002: validate unchanged, accepted by ORCH as read-only (nothing is written or changed); apply-verdict reads, then refuses to write with E_WRITE ELOOP (W13). Why: resolveRunDir (cli.js:37-55) compares paths and checks existence with statSync, which follows links; cli.js and validate.js do not change. (b) Add one bullet to section 11 with the same acceptance, naming ORCH and the date. (c) In the Q11 rows of sections 10 and 12 add: "чтение по ссылке на папку прогона принято (5.4, 11); запись за пределы <root> закрыта (W1.1)". Optional: one fixation row (validate on a symlinked run folder: code 0, strict listing unchanged) so the accepted behaviour cannot change silently.

F2 LOW. Section 9.2 "Строгий список". The return type of tree() is not stated. Existing call sites compare it as a string: apply.reject.test.js:11, apply.state.test.js:16, apply.accept.test.js:70, cli.test.js:37 (assert.equal(tree(a), tree(b))). Fix: state that tree() returns one string, lines joined with "\n", so those four files need no edit.

F3 LOW. Section 9.2 and the existing test cli.test.js:178-183. That test restores the literal 0o644 after chmod 000. With a strict tree that records modes, it passes only under umask 022 (this Mac: 22) and fails under umask 077. Static reading, not run. Fix: one sentence: existing chmod tests restore the mode they read before the chmod.

F4 LOW. Sections 5.7 and 5.6 ("Для ISS-0003"). The label field of writeAllOrNothing targets has no caller in this change (cli.js is unchanged) and no test row: "label" appears only at design lines 711 and 721. Untested code path. Fix: drop label from this change (ISS-0003 adds it with its own test), or add a unit row that calls the helper with a label and checks the <файл> field.

F5 LOW. Sections 5.5, 7, 12 (R2). "Остаток — обычный файл или папка; snapshot их видит" is not exact, because listFiles lists files only. My run on a scratch project: .STATE.md.sai-tmp and runs/.Y.sai-tmp/f (a file inside a temp folder) are listed; an empty runs/.X.sai-tmp is not. The writer's own leftover check still sees an empty temp folder (P1), so there is no safety gap. Fix: reword to "a leftover file, or a temp folder that has a file in it, shows up in snapshot-diff; an empty temp folder does not".

F6 LOW. Sections 5.2 and 5.3 (W3). "STATE.md is replaced last, so if STATE.md holds the new text, the others are new" is false in one corner: when STATE.md already equals the new text and is skipped (W1.5), a SIGKILL between two renames leaves STATE.md "new" (it was before the run) and another target old. The run adds no new inconsistency, but the sentence is stated as general. Fix: "if STATE.md is among the replaced targets, it is replaced last".

F7 LOW. Section 9.4 rows W44, W45, W46 and section 9.5 row P11 (A5 replaced). The added leftover has a modification time nobody can predict, so "tree() = before + that entry" cannot be compared as written. Fix: state that the added entry is compared by type, mode, size and sha256, its mtime excluded, and every other line must equal the "before" listing.

F8 LOW. Section 9.4 row W13, section 9.7 mutant M7. W1.1 checks two folders (runs and runs/<RUN-ID>), but only runs/<RUN-ID> as a link is tested; a mutant that checks only runs/<RUN-ID> survives. Fix: add W13b (RF; runs is a symlink to a folder that holds the run; same expected lines as W13) or say that W13 stands for both.

Not findings. Section 5.6 leaves the code for a mistyped snapshot out-file folder (ISS-0003 case g1) to ISS-0003's design; that path (cli.js:145) is outside this change's write set. The header (lines 9-10) still says CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR has not checked version 4; update it after the verdict.

WHAT PASSED (my own checks)
1. Coverage of criterion 11 (live text). Each clause maps to named rows in 9.1. Precondition and the criterion-4 path note: P12, W18, cli.test.js "STATE.md that is a folder", W13. Targets, STATE.md: W12, W19, W28-W30, W34, W41-W43, W50; proposed-actions.json: W06, W16, W20, W24, W26, W31, W39, W52; apply-report.json: W07-W11, W17, W21, W25, W32, W33, W40, W51; run folder: P05-P07, P09-P11, P13, P14; runs/: P02, P08. Variants: folder W06-W09, link W10-W12, not a regular file W51 (fifo) and W52 (socket); link on the path W13 and P04; file on the path P03. Unreadable: W16, W17. Read-only: W19-W29 and P05, with the no-error controls W22 and W27. Leftovers: W14, W15, W38, P06, and after SIGKILL W47, W48, P13, P14. Every kind of OS error: lstat W50, write W30-W34/P07/P08, chmod W36, link W37, rename W39-W43/P10, mkdir P05/P09, cleanup W44/W46/P11. Both exceptions: W44, W45, P11 and W46. SIGKILL for both commands: W47, W48, P13, P14. P12 for the E_USAGE carve-out. Convergence: A6 and K4. Strict listing: A5 and L01-L09. The check command names three test files, which the test glob of npm run check matches. Mechanical check of the tables (python): 75 rows (W01-W52, P01-P14, L01-L09), each defined once; every id used in 9.1 and 9.7 exists; every target mapping in 9.1 agrees with the row it names, directly or through "как Wxx"; 18 mutants listed.
2. Touched criteria. AC3: E_WRITE of prepare-run is tested in prepare.write.test.js (P03-P11, P13, P14). AC4: existing tests unchanged, P12 added, and the "по пути" reading matches cli.js:37-55. AC6 and AC7: same tests, now with the strict tree (stricter). AC8: the write order changes, but "written" in apply-report.json keeps STATE.md then proposed-actions.json (5.7), so the existing assertion holds. AC9: apply.escalate.test.js unchanged; escalate write failures are W03, W09, W25, W33, W43.
3. No implementation code. Fenced blocks exist only in section 1 (flow), 4.1 and 7 (command lines), 4.1-4.8 (JSON shapes) and the indented STATE.md templates in section 5; none in 5.1-5.7, 6 or 9. No function bodies or control flow. The inline fs calls in 5.3 are the operation list (primitive plus flags), which is what makes the write order unambiguous.
4. Buildable without guessing. Write order, commit point, rollback, temp names, leftover handling and the message catalogue are explicit. Every failing step of W1-W4 and P1-P4 has a catalogue line, one of three outcomes and the extra lines. Exit codes 0, 1, 2. No catch-all: only errors with string code and syscall become E_WRITE, and W49 proves a program error still shows its trace. The line numbers the design cites match the code (apply.js:100-107, prepare.js:36 and :133-138, cli.js:37-55, :71, :145, validate.js:143 and :607-608).
5. Write set. The design changes apply.js, prepare.js, util.js and tools/test/ (helpers.js, fault-inject.js, three new test files). cli.js, validate.js and snapshot.js are unchanged; package.json and eslint.config.js are unchanged; contract.js is not needed. Live tools/src and tools/test equal ORCH's pre-fix manifest (23 files), so nobody has touched code.
6. Quality bar and decisions. Sections 10 and 12 mark every Q1-Q14 and R1-R3 with a reason. No contradiction with decisions/0002 or 0003 (Node 22, no runtime dependency, one check command). The new decision (write strategy) is proposed in 11 and 12 (Q12) for ORCH's decisions/0004. Guards: 5.3 "Охрана — в самой операции" keeps the safety in the operations (wx, rename, exclusive link and mkdir); the check-then-act gaps (a folder becoming a link between W1 and W2) are named and bounded.

PRE-FIX CLAIMS I RE-RAN (scratch copy of the pre-fix tools; TMPDIR in scratch; every spawn with a timeout)
- W51: a fifo as apply-report.json, state RF. Result: status null, SIGTERM, ETIMEDOUT after 4009 ms (4 s timeout), STATE.md changed (f4986d58 to befd98e9), proposed-actions.json created, the fifo still a fifo. Matches the design.
- W34 (M2): state RR, STATE.md padded to 4318 B, /bin/sh -c 'ulimit -f 1; exec node cli.js apply-verdict ...'. Result: exit 1, empty stdout, 8 trace lines, "Error: EFBIG: file too large, write", STATE.md 4318 B down to 1024 B. A re-run without the limit exits 0 here because both markers survived the cut in this fixture (the diagnosis, case C8, saw E_STATE_MARKERS on the larger real file). Matches the design.
- P13: prepare-run killed by SIGKILL inside the write of run.json (preload patching fs.writeFileSync: first half, then SIGKILL). Result: status null, signal SIGKILL; runs/WF06-20260925-01 exists with the copies and a run.json of 517 B; a clean run.json is 1035 B; the next run with the same arguments exits 2, "E_USAGE: run folder already exists". Matches the design (517 of 1035).
- P12: a dangling link at runs/WF06-20260925-01. Result: exit 1, "Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, mkdir '.../runs/WF06-20260925-01/sources/ideas'", 8 trace lines. Matches.
- W13: runs/<RUN-ID> a symlink to a valid run outside <root>. Result: validate exit 0 "OK ... (stage review)"; pre-fix apply-verdict exit 0 "applied recommend", STATE.md changed, proposed-actions.json and apply-report.json created outside <root>, the link still a link. Matches the design; it is also the evidence for F1.
- Fixture sizes after a clean first apply: STATE.md 1066 B, proposed-actions.json 353 B, apply-report.json 419 B; run.json 1035 B (as in 9.2 and 9.5).
Facts the fix depends on (Node v22.21.1, umask 022). A hard link renamed back restores the same inode, mtime (ns), mode and bytes, with no leftover. wx, linkSync and mkdirSync on an existing name give EEXIST. access W_OK on a 0444 file gives EACCES. Rename of a file over a folder gives EISDIR; of a folder over a non-empty folder, ENOTEMPTY; over an empty folder it replaces. Rename over a dangling link replaces the link silently, so the W1.2 refusal is needed. A temp file in a 555 folder gives EACCES while an in-place write of an existing file there succeeds, so the read-only-folder refusal is really new. A wx file gets the same mode as a plainly created one.
